messages.author: 16e54b204be777c6
messages.subject: passing arguments to xtable
parts:
I am having trouble getting arguments that are passed to xtable() to be reactive.  I think an example will help.

Below are the ui.R and server.R files (I tried to attach them, but kept getting an error when trying to post). This app has a sliderInput and tableOutput.  The slider is supposed to let the user control how many digits to use in the tableOutput.  However, changing the slider has no effect.

Note that this App does NOT work on the current development version; with the development version it gives this error.
Error in http_response(ws, status = response$status, content_type = response$content_type,  : 
  unused argument(s) (headers = response$headers)


That error does not occur with the version installed from http://rstudio.org/_packages, although the slider input does not work as I had hoped.


#This is the ui.R script:

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("test"),

  sidebarPanel( 
    wellPanel(
      sliderInput(inputId='digits', label='Digits', min=1, max=10, step=1, 
                  value=5)
    )
  ),

  mainPanel(
    tableOutput(outputId = "mydata")
  )
))


## This is the server.R script

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  makeData <- reactive(function() {
    invalidateLater(1000)
    data.frame(A=rnorm(10), B=rnorm(10))
  })
  
  output$mydata <- reactiveTable(function() {
    makeData()
  }, digits=input$digits)
})

#---------------------------------------------

Regards,
Garrett

messages.author: f806781d102fe0ab
messages.subject: Re: passing arguments to xtable
parts:
The http_response error was due to an outdated version of websockets (1.1.6 is now required).

The reason the digits don't change as you move the slider is because digits=input$digits is only resolved once, at the time that reactiveTable is called. In other words, the arguments you pass to reactiveTable aren't themselves magically reactive. However, you could work around this by wrapping the entire call to reactiveTable in another reactive function:



  output$mydata <- reactive(function() {



    reactiveTable(function() {



      makeData()


    }, digits=input$digits, caption="hello", caption.placement='top')()



  })

It's a little kludgy looking but will work just fine.
